_note: Tank journal for the app (v1.12+). One entry per test, matched to tank_water_log.csv by tank_id + date + time. Joseph adds an entry with every new test. Fields: title, meaning, actions (list), notes.

entries.title: Fishless start: nothing feeding the bacteria
entries.meaning: No fish and no bottled ammonia, so the bacteria had no food. Ammonia and nitrite at 0 here meant the cycle was not moving, not that it was done. Nitrate 10 most likely came from the plant soil.
actions: Add ammonia to about 2 ppm (dropped that evening when fish went in)
Keep dosing 20 ml Nite-Out II daily
Test the tap water to explain the nitrate
entries.notes: Nite-Out II 20 ml (day 2). Status corrected WATCH to ACTION under the fishless rules (Wayne approved).

entries.title: First test with fish; KH and pH fell overnight
entries.meaning: 4 zebra danios and 3 platys went in on the evening of 10/04, so this is now a fish-in cycle and the fish supply the ammonia. KH dropped 80 to 40 and pH 6.8 to 6.2 overnight. Tap water is KH 180 and pH 7.8, so the plant soil is pulling them down.
actions: 25% water change today with 4 ml Fraction
Retest pH and KH tomorrow morning
New rule: KH under 60 means a 25% change that day
entries.notes: Tap baseline 10/04: pH 7.8, KH 180, GH 125, chlorine 0.5, nitrate 0.

entries.title: Evening recheck: KH and pH holding low
entries.meaning: KH 40 and pH 6.2 did not fall further, but did not recover either. Nitrate 10 to 5 with no water change is strip variation. Fish active and lively.
actions: Do the 25% water change tonight (4 ml Fraction)
Re-anchor the uprooted plants
Retest pH and KH in the morning
entries.notes: Nite-Out II 20 ml.

entries.title: pH stuck at 6.2, KH on the WATCH line
entries.meaning: Third pH 6.2 in a row. KH 40 is one step from ACTION. Ammonia and nitrite still 0 on day 4: the early part of the cycle, waste has not built up yet. The planned 10/05 water change was not done.
actions: 25% water change today (4 ml Fraction)
Retest pH and KH tomorrow morning
entries.notes: Nite-Out II 20 ml after the test.

entries.title: Cycle has started: ammonia and nitrite showing
entries.meaning: First readings above 0: ammonia 0.5 and nitrite about 0.5 (strip shows somewhere between 0 and 1). The bacteria are starting to grow. KH about 20 is crash territory.
actions: Water change tonight, not tomorrow: 25% now and 25% more later, 4 ml Fraction each
Skip feeding tonight
Get crushed coral for steadier KH
entries.notes: Heater turned down (79.7°F). 4 ml Fraction dosed about 18:20 as a stopgap; no water change done.

entries.title: Ammonia cleared overnight; nitrite still up
entries.meaning: Ammonia 0.5 to 0 overnight: the ammonia-eating bacteria are working, helped by the Fraction. Nitrite still about 0.5, which is the second stage of the cycle. KH about 20 is still ACTION.
actions: 25% water change now and another this evening, 4 ml Fraction each
Skip feeding or feed very lightly
Full test tomorrow morning
entries.notes: Nite-Out II 20 ml. Temp back to 77°F.

entries.title: One 50% water change fixed everything
entries.meaning: Nitrite 0.5 to 0, pH 6.2 to 7.2, KH about 20 to 80, GH 125. Tap water is the dependable way to bring KH back.
actions: No more water changes tonight
Full test tomorrow morning
Feed lightly if nitrite is still 0
Keep dosing 20 ml Nite-Out II
entries.notes: 50% change about 20:00 with about 5 ml Fraction. Plants re-anchored and zeolite root tabs added; about 11 to 15 plants. Water went cloudy afterward.

entries.title: KH crashed again overnight
entries.meaning: KH 80 to 40 and pH 7.2 to 6.2 in about 10 hours: the soil pulls KH down fast. Ammonia and nitrite both 0, which is good. GH 125 to 50 is probably the strip.
actions: 25% water change today (4 ml Fraction)
Feed lightly
Crushed coral is now a priority
entries.notes: Nite-Out II 20 ml. The water change was not done.

entries.title: KH and pH held; water milky
entries.meaning: KH 80 and pH 6.8 with no water change, so one of the last two strip reads was probably off. Ammonia and nitrite 0 for the second morning. Milky white water is a bacterial bloom: harmless, clears on its own.
actions: No water change today
Leave the cloudy water alone (no clarifier)
Feed lightly; full test tomorrow
entries.notes: Fish swimming normally, good color. Crushed coral not stocked locally; ordered online.

entries.title: Third morning of zeros
entries.meaning: Ammonia and nitrite 0 for three mornings after the spike: the tank is finishing its cycle. KH and pH held a second night. The bloom is clearing.
actions: No water change today
Feed lightly
Full test tomorrow morning
entries.notes: Nite-Out II 20 ml. Temp 76.4°F, on target.

entries.title: Up to 12 new fish added; KH dropped
entries.meaning: The fish load jumped from 7 to as many as 19 in the middle of the cycle, without quarantine. More fish means more waste and faster KH use. The week-of-zeros clock restarts, so the earliest the tank can be called cycled is about 10/17.
actions: 25% water change tonight (4 ml Fraction)
Skip feeding tonight
No more fish until the tank is cycled
Watch new fish for white spots, clamped or torn fins
entries.notes: New fish include at least one angelfish, more zebra danios, and more platys.

entries.title: Zeros hold with the bigger fish load
entries.meaning: Ammonia and nitrite 0 the first morning with about 19 fish: the bacteria are keeping up. KH 40 and pH 6.2 unchanged because the planned water change was skipped.
actions: 25% water change today (4 ml Fraction)
Feed a small pinch only
Watch closely for ammonia or nitrite
entries.notes: Two of the new fish are dwarf gouramis. Nite-Out II dosed (amount not stated).

entries.title: KH down to 20
entries.meaning: KH has been 40 or lower since 10/10 with no water change and is now in pH-crash territory. Ammonia and nitrite still 0, fifth morning in a row.
actions: 50% water change today with 5 ml Fraction (or two 25% changes, 4 ml each)
Nite-Out II already in; don't re-dose
Small pinch of food; full test tomorrow
entries.notes: New rule: KH under 40 means a 50% change that day. Nite-Out II 20 ml.

entries.title: Back in range after a 50% change (without Fraction)
entries.meaning: KH 20 to 80, pH 6.2 to 6.8, GH 50 to 125: same lift as the 10/07 change. Nite-Out II went in by mistake instead of Fraction. Chlorine read 0, but the strip can't see under 0.5 and doesn't read chloramine.
actions: Dose 5 ml Fraction tonight if it hasn't gone in
Watch for an ammonia or nitrite bump over the next 1 to 3 days
Fraction goes in with new water; Nite-Out II after. Not interchangeable
entries.notes: Facebook group feedback: the plant soil is the KH drain and water changes are the fix; crushed coral helps but isn't reliable on its own.

entries.title: KH held overnight; bacteria unharmed
entries.meaning: KH 80 and pH 6.8 held after yesterday's change, unlike 10/08. Ammonia and nitrite 0 for the 6th morning, 3rd with about 19 fish, so the unconditioned change did not hurt the bacteria. Nitrate still 0 on 6 tests; it needs to show before calling the tank cycled. GH 50 is probably the strip.
actions: No water change today
Dose 20 ml Nite-Out II and feed a small pinch
Full test tomorrow morning: KH under 60 means 25% change, under 40 means 50%
entries.notes: Earliest the tank can be called cycled: about 10/17. Temp back to 77.3°F.

entries.title: 7th morning of zeros; KH 180 looks like a strip misread
entries.meaning: Ammonia and nitrite 0 for the 7th morning, 4th with about 19 fish, and no delayed hit from the 10/12 change. KH jumped 80 to 180 overnight with no water change or coral, and the pad was uneven (green with yellow), so it is probably the strip; KH is fine either way. Nitrate still 0 on 7 tests.
actions: No water change today
Dose 20 ml Nite-Out II and feed a small pinch
Tomorrow: fresh strip, dip 1-2 seconds, read KH at the time on the bottle
entries.notes: Fish active and coming to the front. Water a little milky but maybe better. Floating plants growing long roots. Earliest cycled call: about 10/17, once nitrate shows.

entries.title: Evening: KH back to 40, so this morning's 180 was a misread
entries.meaning: Ammonia and nitrite are still 0 with all the fish. KH 40 tonight means the morning's 180 was a bad strip read; the real drop is 80 to 40 since yesterday, the plant soil pulling KH down as expected. pH held at 6.8 so far.
actions: 25% water change tonight with 4 ml Fraction (Fraction, not Nite-Out II)
Small pinch of food
Full test tomorrow morning with a fresh strip, dipped 1-2 s and read on time
entries.notes: GH 50 to 125 since morning with no water change (strip variation). Nitrate 0 for the 8th test. 78.2°F.

entries.title: 8th morning of 0/0; KH stuck at 40 and pH back to 6.2
entries.meaning: Ammonia and nitrite are still 0 with all the fish: 5 mornings with the full load, and the 10/12 unconditioned water change did no harm. KH stayed at 40 overnight and pH fell from 6.8 to 6.2, the same state as 10/11, right before KH hit 20. The plant soil is still pulling KH down.
actions: 50% water change today with 5 ml Fraction (Fraction, not Nite-Out II)
20 ml Nite-Out II after the change; small pinch of food
Full test tomorrow morning
Watch the angelfish's fin tips for more fraying
entries.notes: Water looks clearer in today's photos. Nitrate 0 for the 9th test (floaters using it). GH 125 to 50 (strip). 77.9°F. Last night's 25% change was not reported.

entries.title: Cycle done: 9th morning of 0/0; KH still stuck at 40
entries.meaning: Ammonia and nitrite have read 0 on every test for a week with all the fish in, and they stayed 0 even with no Nite-Out II for a few days. The bacteria are established, so the cycle is done (nitrate stays at 0 because the floating plants use it). KH is still 40 and pH 6.2, the same as 10/15: the plant soil keeps pulling them down, and last time this led to KH 20.
actions: 50% water change today with 5 ml Fraction (Fraction, not Nite-Out II)
No need to buy more Nite-Out II
Normal small feeding once a day
Full test tomorrow morning (KH and pH matter most now)
Put the crushed coral in the canister when it arrives
entries.notes: 10/16 test missed. GH 50 to 125 (strip). 77.3°F. No water change since the last one; no Fraction dosed. Hold off on new fish until KH is steady and the fish are counted.

entries.title: KH still 40 after a 6-gallon change
entries.meaning: Yesterday's 6-gallon change (about 15%) was too small to move KH or pH: both read exactly the same as before (KH 40, pH 6.2). The plant soil keeps pulling KH down about as fast as a small change adds it. Ammonia and nitrite are still 0, so the cycle is holding.
actions: 20-gallon (50%) water change today with 4 ml Fraction; two 10-gallon rounds is fine
Small normal feeding
Full test tomorrow morning (KH and pH)
Put the crushed coral in the canister when it arrives
entries.notes: 6-gal change with Fraction 10/17 ~13:00. Nitrate 0 (11th test). GH 125. 77.3°F. No Nite-Out II (not needed).

entries.title: KH hit 0 - water change today
entries.meaning: KH (alkalinity) is the buffer that holds pH steady, and it has now run out. The plant soil keeps eating it. With no buffer, pH can drop fast and stress the fish. pH reads 6.2, the lowest step on the strip, so it may already be lower. Ammonia and nitrite are still 0, so the cycle is fine and the fish look normal.
actions: 50% (20-gallon) water change today with 4-5 ml Fraction; match the temperature
Starting tonight: 1/2 tsp baking soda dissolved in a cup of tank water, poured in slowly, once a day (max 1 tsp/day) until the crushed coral is in
Full test tomorrow morning (KH and pH first)
Wipe the green specks off the front glass with the magnet cleaner
entries.notes: 10/19 test missed. 20-gal change advised 10/18 not reported. Nitrate 0 (12th test). GH 125. 77.9°F. Green dust/spot algae starting on the glass - normal for a new planted tank.

entries.title: Nitrite back (1) with KH still 0; shrimp added
entries.meaning: First nitrite since 10/07 after nine clean tests. Most likely a small bump from the extra bioload (new shrimp) on bacteria working in very soft, acidic water: with KH 0 and pH at or below 6.2, the nitrite-eating bacteria slow right down. Nitrate 10 is the first above 0 in two weeks, so the chain is still running. Fish look healthy. Shrimp are more sensitive than the fish to nitrite and to low KH/pH. The last confirmed water change was 10/17 (only 15%), so the soil has had almost a week to drain the buffer.
actions: 50% water change today with 5 ml Fraction (Fraction also detoxifies nitrite)
Start or keep up 1/2 tsp baking soda per day, dissolved, poured slowly
Skip feeding today, then light feeding
Full test tomorrow morning: nitrite, KH, pH first
Put the crushed coral in as soon as it arrives
No more new animals until nitrite is 0 and KH holds
entries.notes: Small shrimp added (species and count not stated). Tests 10/21-10/22 not reported. The 50% change advised 10/20 was not done (Wayne, 07:43); planned for today. Juvenile fish growing; algae on glass under control.

entries.title: KH and pH back up after the 50% change; nitrite still 1
entries.meaning: Last night's 50% change brought KH from 0 back up to 80 and pH from 6.2 up to 6.8, so the buffer is restored. Nitrite didn't move, though. The bacteria that clear nitrite slowed down while the water was so acidic, and they need a few days to catch up. Nitrite damages the fish's blood so it carries less oxygen, and shrimp are hit harder. Each water change takes out about half of it.
actions: Another 50% water change today with 5 ml Fraction. Why: the change cuts nitrite in half, and Fraction binds what's left until the bacteria catch up
Feed lightly, a small pinch once a day. Why: less food means less waste becoming nitrite
Full test tomorrow morning. Why: to see whether nitrite is falling
No baking soda needed. Why: KH 80 is in the good range
entries.notes: 50% change done the evening of 10/23. Baking soda was never used. Wayne pointed out it was suggested without a reason, which is fair, and the team now gives a reason with every step.

entries.title: Nitrite fading (lighter pink); shrimp alive; snail seen
entries.meaning: The nitrite pad is lighter pink than before, so nitrite is probably between 0 and 1 and dropping. The strip can't show anything between those two steps. The bacteria are catching up. KH held at 80, which means the buffer from the water change lasted. pH reading 6.2 with KH 80 doesn't add up, since that much buffer normally keeps pH near 7. One-day pH drops on strips are often a bad read, so check it again tomorrow. Nitrate went from 10 to 0, which fits yesterday's 50% change. At least one shrimp is alive. The snail is most likely a bladder or pond snail that rode in on the plants. It's harmless and eats algae and leftovers.
actions: 50% water change today with 5 ml Fraction. Why: nitrite is still showing, and each change cuts it about in half while the bacteria finish catching up
Keep feeding lightly. Why: less waste means less nitrite for the bacteria to deal with
Test tomorrow morning, nitrite first. Why: one more lighter reading, or a 0, means the bump is over
Leave the snails alone. Why: they're cleanup crew. A sudden snail boom means too much food, so it doubles as a feeding gauge
entries.notes: 50% change done 10/24 (Wayne confirmed), the second in a row. Green spot algae specks on the front glass (wipe during the change). Snail ID is Joseph's, not confirmed.

entries.title: Nitrite almost gone; KH slipping back to 40
entries.meaning: Nitrite is lighter again, between 0 and 1 and dropping day by day, so the bacteria are winning. KH fell from 80 to 40 in a day. That's the plant soil pulling the buffer down, the same pattern as before. pH 6.8 is better, and it suggests yesterday's 6.2 was a bad read.
actions: 50% water change today with 5 ml Fraction. Why: it should clear the last of the nitrite and put KH back up to about 80. Your tap water is KH 180, and KH 40 is the line where pH can start to slide
Keep feeding lightly. Why: less waste while the bacteria finish catching up
Test tomorrow morning, nitrite and KH first. Why: nitrite at 0 means the bump is over, and KH shows how fast the soil is pulling it down
Crushed coral when it arrives. Why: it's the only thing that holds KH up between water changes
entries.notes: Nitrite logged as 0.5, an estimate (the strip only has 0 and 1). Whether the 10/25 change was done is not reported.
